title: A workspace or a group of workspaces can be put to sleep and woken
body:
When the server stops, `save.rs` writes each workspace's layout, and on the next start the panes come back empty and pinned terminals restart in their saved directories. Programs in panes cost memory and CPU while their workspace sits unused, and today the only way to free that is to close the workspace or stop the server.

## Proposal

Sleeping a workspace puts it in the state a server stop would leave it in, while the server and the other workspaces keep running:

- Sleep saves the workspace's layout, asks its windows to close, and kills the programs decade started in it. The panes stay, empty.
- A sleeping workspace shows its empty panes with a wake button. Switching to it does not wake it.
- Wake runs the restore path for that one workspace: pinned terminals restart in their saved directories.
- A sleeping workspace stays asleep when the server restarts. The save file gains a flag for it, which bumps the format's version byte, and the reader keeps an arm for the old layout.
- Sleeping a workspace whose agent is working asks first.
- A group's right-click menu offers Sleep and Wake for every workspace in it.

## Cost

Sleep is as good as restore. Shells come back fresh, without scrollback or what ran in them. An agent session in a pane comes back only with decade-cf942a, and GUI apps only with decade-15e5eb.

## Rejected

- Freezing with SIGSTOP and SIGCONT. It wakes instantly with everything intact, but frees no memory unless the system swaps, and network connections such as an agent's may time out while stopped. Jack chose not to take it on now.

## Open

- Where the wake button and a sleeping card's look go, in the sidebar and on the pane placeholder.
- Whether to sleep a workspace by itself after a time unused. Left until manual sleep has been used.

Jack answered the design questions on 2026-11-21.
